wesleyan-freeman-asian-scholars-2027.about:
The Freeman Asian Scholarship Program, created in 1995 with the Freeman Foundation and now funded by Wesleyan itself, brings exceptionally promising Asian students to Wesleyan University in Connecticut, a leading US liberal arts university. Each Freeman Scholar receives a scholarship covering the full cost of attendance for four years: tuition, fees, room and board, supplies, and travel to and from the home country, worth over US$100,000.

Citizens and permanent residents of China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam who apply to Wesleyan as financial-aid-seeking candidates are considered automatically. Around 11 students are chosen each year, so it is extremely competitive: selection looks at academic achievement, intellectual curiosity, discipline, personal qualities, community involvement, leadership and English ability. Interviews are not part of selection (optional InitialView interviews are accepted), and Wesleyan is test-optional but encourages SAT/ACT from non-exam-based curricula.

Apply through the Common App by 1 January 2027 (Regular Decision, when most Freeman offers are made) or by an Early Decision deadline, with Wesleyan's international financial aid documents.

stanford-summer-session-high-school-2027.about:
Stanford Summer Session lets high-school sophomores, juniors and seniors study alongside Stanford and visiting university students for eight weeks. Students choose from 130+ regular courses across disciplines (computer science, engineering, mathematics, psychology, economics, writing and more), take at least 8 units if residential, and receive grades and an official Stanford transcript.

utwente-itc-excellence-scholarship-2027.about:
The Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) at the University of Twente is a world centre for remote sensing, GIS and spatial planning, with a long history of training professionals from developing countries.

The ITC Excellence Scholarship gives €25,000 plus an ITC tuition waiver of €33,180 for the two-year Master's in Geo-information Science and Earth Observation or the Master's in Spatial Engineering. It is partial: with total costs estimated at €75,680, you contribute about €17,500 for the rest of tuition, living allowance, insurance and residence permit. To continue into year two, you need at least 45 of 60 EC.

Applicants must be nationals and residents of one of about 150 eligible countries, be in the top 10% academically, have IELTS 6.5 and hold academic admission before applying. The 2027 application deadline is 1 March 2027.
highlights: €25,000 scholarship + €33,180 tuition waiver
Remote sensing, GIS and spatial engineering
Deadline 1 March 2027
utwente-itc-excellence-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Nationals and residents of an eligible country (about 150, including Afghanistan, Brazil, India, Kenya, Mexico, Nigeria, Ukraine and Vietnam; check the list for Georgia), academic admission to the eligible ITC master's, non-Dutch bachelor's, top 10% of class, IELTS 6.5 overall, first enrolment at UT, ability to pay the own contribution, and no other full scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply for academic admission to the ITC master's via the UT online system
Wait for the acceptance letter
Complete the ITC Excellence Scholarship form with required documents
Submit by 1 March 2027 and plan for the €17,500 own contribution
utwente-itc-excellence-scholarship-2027.costs: Scholarship €25,000 + tuition waiver €33,180. Own contribution about €17,500 (tuition remainder, living, insurance, residence permit) of an estimated €75,680 total for two years.

si-pioneering-women-in-stem-2027.about:
The Swedish Institute's Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship funds women with leadership experience to take selected English-taught STEM master's programmes at Swedish universities. It is separate from the SI Scholarship for Global Professionals and targets ten countries: Bangladesh, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, the Philippines, Rwanda, South Africa, Thailand and Vietnam.

The scholarship pays full tuition directly to the university, a monthly allowance of SEK 12,000 and a one-off travel grant of SEK 15,000, plus membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals. Applicants need documented work and leadership experience (from a job, entrepreneurship or civil society) and must not already hold an SI scholarship or a Swedish degree.

The process has two steps: apply to an eligible master's on universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027, then submit the SI application between 8 and 24 February 2027. The list of eligible programmes and application documents is published on 13 November 2026.
highlights: Full tuition + SEK 12,000/month + SEK 15,000 travel grant
For women STEM leaders from 10 African and Asian countries
SI portal open 8–24 February 2027
si-pioneering-women-in-stem-2027.eligibility: Female citizens of Bangladesh, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, the Philippines, Rwanda, South Africa, Thailand or Vietnam (residence elsewhere allowed), liable to pay Swedish tuition fees, applying to an eligible STEM master's, with documented work and leadership experience, and without a previous SI scholarship or Swedish degree. Not open to Georgian or Qatari citizens.
how_to_apply: Check the eligible master's programmes published on 13 November 2026
Apply to the programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and keep your application number
Prepare the SI application documents listed on the SI page (including proof of work and leadership experience)
Submit the SI application between 8 and 24 February 2027 (closes 14:59 CET)
si-pioneering-women-in-stem-2027.costs: Full tuition paid by SI to the university, SEK 12,000 per month living allowance, one-time SEK 15,000 travel grant (not for those already in Sweden), and SI network membership.

kamun-2026.about:
Karlsruhe Model United Nations is run by the student association MUNIKA e.V. and held at KIT, one of Germany's leading technical universities. Committees such as UNESCO, WHO and the Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space are grouped by difficulty, so high-school students and university students can each find the right room.

The conference runs 13–15 November 2026 in Karlsruhe, Germany at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) and is aimed at high school and university students. Working language: English. Committees: Committees by level (highschooler, beginner, intermediate, expert, university), e.g. UNESCO (heritage in conflict zones), WHO (future pandemics), COPUOS (cooperation in space exploration).

Choose a committee on the official site and sign up directly from the committee card. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

Hosted at KIT; committees sorted by level
Committees: Committees by level (highschooler, beginner, intermediate, expert, university), e.g. UNESCO (heritage in conflict zones), WHO (future pandemics), COPUOS (cooperation in space exploration)

Pay the delegation and delegate fees by the published deadline to confirm your places.
Receive your country and committee allocation, research your country's position and submit a position paper if required.
Arrange travel, visa (if needed) and accommodation, then attend the opening ceremony and committee sessions.
